unresolvedReleaseQuestions.question: Whether § 311.326 requires a hearing. The section says that if the court determines, upon review, that the conditions are met, the court shall enter an order of expungement — upon review rather than after hearing, which is the wording § 610.130.2 uses. On its face no hearing is required, which would make this the only Missouri petition route without one, but the section does not forbid one and Missouri courts may set one as a matter of practice. The packet tells the participant to ask the clerk rather than promising either way.

Whether a conviction under a municipal or county underage-possession ordinance, rather than under § 311.325 itself, is within § 311.326. The section names the statute and the packet applies the narrower reading, which excludes ordinance convictions; but many Missouri underage-drinking cases are charged municipally, so the narrower reading takes a substantial population out of the route. Unresolved on the face of the section.

Whether any Missouri circuit, associate or municipal division publishes a local form for a § 311.326 expungement, notwithstanding that the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes none. A June 2024 Missouri pro se guide lists § 311.326 among the statutes for which no Missouri court forms are prepared and directs the reader to draft their own petition. Local publication is not excluded and the track carries localFormOverride for that reason.
Which FI-05 case type code a § 311.326 application takes where a new case is opened. The published Case Types List names no code for the section. The code is left blank and confirmed with the clerk.

Whether any Missouri circuit or municipal division publishes a local form for a § 610.130 expungement, notwithstanding that the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes none. Two independent Missouri sources confirm no statewide form exists — the 16th Judicial Circuit's informational sheet says there are no forms provided and the applicant or their attorney must draft and file all pleadings, and a June 2024 pro se guide lists § 610.130 among the statutes with no Missouri court forms prepared. Local publication is not excluded and the track carries localFormOverride for that reason.

Which FI-05 case type code a § 610.130 application takes where a new case is opened. The official Case Types List publishes only XG, X5 and X# for expungement and none of them names this section. The code is left blank and confirmed with the clerk rather than guessed from a similar track name.

Who gives notice of the § 610.130 hearing, and to whom. The section requires a hearing but prescribes no notice recipients, no objection window and no service rule, unlike §§ 610.140.6 and 610.123.3 which do all three. Whether the clerk notices the prosecutor as on the § 610.140 routes, or the applicant serves the named respondents, is local practice. The packet includes a certificate of service the participant completes only if the clerk so directs.
